should_trigger.prompt: will the team understand this handoff doc without me there to explain it?
check that this runbook is self-contained before I publish it
review this ticket for completeness before I send it to the contractor
does this README make sense to someone who's never seen the project?
about to send this SOP to the offshore team — will it stand alone without me?
fresh-eyes pass on my design doc before tomorrow's handoff meeting
will this make sense to someone who wasn't in any of our conversations?
should_trigger.note: situation phrasing: describes the circumstance without reusing the description's routing vocabulary — tests under-triggering, the axis lexical overlap hides

should_not_trigger.prompt: review my code before I merge
proofread this for grammar and typos
score the argument quality of this essay
cut this doc down by half
should we migrate our monolith to microservices?
should_not_trigger.note: near-boundary: falsification-review's own trigger phrasing — cold-read declares this out of scope, so it must not claim it

effectiveness.task: Read this plan as a TypeScript service engineer who must implement it: 'Add POST /exports accepting {accountId: string}. Return 202 with {jobId: string}; return 404 for an unknown account and 409 when an active export exists. Open decision: the product owner must decide whether callers can export another account. Choose private helper names locally. Start in src/exports.ts, which exists. Completion: tests cover accepted requests and both errors.' Audit readiness without rewriting or resolving the product decision.
effectiveness.success_criteria: Identifies the cross-account authorization decision as an execution blocker despite its explicit owner; recognizes the stated first action and completion checks; does not flag unspecified private helper names; does not invent the missing policy or turn the audit into a design correctness review.

effectiveness.task: Audit this runbook for an on-call engineer: the introduction says 'Rotate the token using the control-plane steps below.' A later section defines control plane as the internal admin console, links the console URL, names the required operator role, gives the rotation steps and rollback, and defines success as a successful request with the replacement token. The engineer ordinarily knows HTTP. Review the whole artifact before reporting gaps.
effectiveness.success_criteria: Does not flag control plane as undefined because its definition occurs later; does not demand a definition of HTTP; checks whether the console link and role are usable within available scope; does not manufacture blockers from ordinary audience knowledge.
